input.quote: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
input.rationale: Section 13.1 is the operative Services licence and fails the fallback on two material terms: it expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them (walk-away territory under the rule), and it is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Sections 13.2 and 13.3 do not cure this — 13.2 reaches only paid-up or embedded software and Vendor Technology, not the Services, and while 13.3 constrains revocation and permits Affiliate/successor transfer, it does not extend the Services grant to Affiliates or contractors. The redline aligns 13.1 with the model already agreed in 13.2/13.3 (Affiliates and contractors covered; revocation only on material uncured breach after notice and cure; transfer to an Affiliate or successor), reaching the preferred position with a single-sentence edit.

proposal.summary: Extend Services licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocation at Vendor's discretion
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Services licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and replaced revocation at Vendor's sole discretion with the notice-and-cure standard already agreed in Section 13.3. Our playbook requires operational use by affiliates and contractors and a licence that cannot be pulled at will; if helpful we can instead cover Affiliates on written notice as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
ops.newText: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a licence to use the Services, revocable or suspendable only as permitted by Section 13.3 and transferable to an Affiliate or successor in accordance with Section 13.3.
